chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, that he said: I asked Abu al-Hasan, the Last, peace be upon him, about the sincere repentance: What is it?
So he, peace be upon him, wrote: That the internal is like the apparent and (even) better than that.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of sincere repentance (Tawbah Nusuh) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Hassan al-Askari (peace be upon him) defines sincere repentance (*tawbah al-nusuh*) as the alignment of the inner self with the outward appearance, ensuring no hidden sins remain concealed. The Imam further notes that true sincerity transcends mere consistency, implying a profound, enduring state of purity that prevents the recurrence of sin. This definition aligns with the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) as a continuous spiritual state rather than a singular event.
